trigger: a command_dedup.db that opens but whose quick_check fails, e.g. one damaged page after a power loss
policy_floor: catastrophic-if-violated clause in the Durable agent command idempotency row of .claude/routed-concerns.md: an IN-FLIGHT row is NEVER evicted (docs/command-dedup.md invariant 5)
classification_rationale: the docs claimed the recovery was no worse than staying degraded; for a file that still opens that is false
summary: Quarantining on a PRAGMA quick_check failure alone discards ALL dedup history, including in-flight claims, from a file that still opens and mostly works (reviewer measured 2988 of 3000 ids still resolving after one damaged page). Violates docs/command-dedup.md invariants 4 and 5. Native MEDIUM, derived HIGH (the derived band governs). Fixed in c4aa020c2 by OWNER RULING R1: no integrity scan; quarantine only when the file cannot be opened. New test proves a file that opens with a damaged data page is NOT quarantined.

trigger: a sustained media fault or crash-looping boot
classification_rationale: retention behaviour of a new on-disk artefact
summary: Quarantined files (up to a ring of saved responses) were never pruned, so a disk that corrupts the file on every boot leaves one per boot forever. Fixed in c4aa020c2 by OWNER RULING R2: keep the newest 3 (count-based; the just-created file is exempt).

trigger: an operator relies on the counter to find endpoints that lost history
classification_rationale: docs implied yuzu_agent_dedup_quarantined_total was operator-visible; the agent has no /metrics endpoint
summary: The new counter is endpoint-local and the docs implied otherwise; security-guardian independently raised the same gap (invariant 7: MUST stay observable). Fixed in c4aa020c2: heartbeat tag yuzu.dedup_quarantined, docs say it is a per-process value.

trigger: a reader trusts the comment; a future edit adds an early return between acquire and release
classification_rationale: a comment overclaimed; moved manual close/free judged pre-existing cleanup in a touched file (SHOULD-class, not the floor)
summary: (F4) the 'can never replay a stale WAL' comment overclaimed; (F5) the manual sqlite3_close on a failed open_v2 and sqlite3_free(err_msg) were MOVED not added. Fixed in c4aa020c2: comment softened, DbGuard constructed before the rc check (DbCloser is null-safe, verified by cpp-safety), sqlite3_errmsg replaces err_msg.

trigger: a reader of the docs
classification_rationale: timestamp vs unix-epoch naming, sidecar wording, 'never overwriting' overstatement, unnumbered 'tracked follow-up', vague 'cousin' comment
summary: Five wording nits from the round-1 docs review, all fixed in c4aa020c2 / d04ccdc4c (the never-overwriting overstatement was closed in substance by the atomic name claim).

trigger: damage confined to the meta table pages (pages 4 and 5 of the file) of an otherwise intact store
policy_floor: catastrophic-if-violated clause in the Durable agent command idempotency row of .claude/routed-concerns.md: an IN-FLIGHT row is NEVER evicted (docs/command-dedup.md invariant 5)
classification_rationale: the schema step's INSERT INTO meta probes the meta table's own pages
summary: The INSERT INTO meta ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in the schema exec probes the meta table's b-tree pages, which command_outcomes never uses. Damage confined to them returned SQLITE_CORRUPT -> corrupt=true -> a file whose command table was fully readable (3000/3000 rows, verified at the SQL level) was quarantined, discarding in-flight claims (owner ruling R1, invariants 4 and 5). THE TWO REVIEWERS DISAGREED ON THE BAND: architect derived HIGH (absolute), the security re-review derived LOW/INFO (relative: the pre-change code failed open() outright on that same file). Fixed regardless in c97b50b13: the exec is split, only creating the two tables can mark a file corrupt, the seed is warn-and-continue; new test damages meta pages 4 and 5 and asserts nothing is quarantined and all 100 ids resolve. Architect re-confirmed closed; enterprise-architect final review confirmed closed.

trigger: a foreign file name that cannot be narrowed (Windows) or bad_alloc
classification_rationale: the comment and ledger said 'never throws'; the code could throw out of non-noexcept open() after a successful recovery
summary: prune_old_quarantines could throw (path::string() on a foreign name, bad_alloc) out of open() AFTER recovery succeeded; the agent boot path has no try/catch, so a best-effort tidy-up could turn a recovery into a boot failure. Reported independently by cpp-safety, cpp-expert and the security re-review. Fixed in c97b50b13: noexcept with a function-level try/catch(...) that logs; test 'prune never throws on a missing directory'.

trigger: a local actor (or accident) creates a sign-shaped name in the data directory
classification_rationale: documented grammar was digits-only; from_chars into long long accepts a leading '-'
summary: Names like command_dedup.db.corrupt--0 and ...corrupt-5--0 parsed as quarantine groups. Fixed in c97b50b13: parse_digits requires ASCII digits only; grammar table test (sign, plus, overflow, double suffix, whitespace). Reported by cpp-safety and the security re-review.

trigger: any change to quarantine_corrupt_db's sidecar loop
classification_rationale: the test name claimed behaviour its assertions sat inside a never-true if
summary: SQLite itself truncates a garbage -wal when the failed attempt closes, so the stale-WAL test's content checks never ran; the non-empty-sidecar, empty-sidecar and rename-fail branches were untested. cpp-safety raised the same gap. Fixed in c97b50b13 by moving the filesystem half into command_dedup_quarantine.hpp and driving it directly (sidecars travel / empty removed / -n collisions / pre-1970 clamp / name grammar / bystanders / symlink); the old test renamed honestly. The unmovable-sidecar rename-fail-then-remove arm remains untested.

trigger: the wall clock is before 1970 during a recovery, repeatedly
classification_rationale: a pre-1970 clock wrote .corrupt--5, which the parser rejects
summary: A negative epoch produced a quarantine name parse_quarantine_name rejects, so the file was never pruned and the keep-3 rule did not cover it. Fixed in c97b50b13: the epoch is clamped to >= 0; test.

trigger: a regression in the classification of transient errors, or moving prune back inside if (attempt)
classification_rationale: missing coverage for the owner's 'transient is not corruption' and 'second attempt fails' questions
summary: Transient-not-corruption was tested only by CANTOPEN on a directory; the branch 'quarantine succeeded, then the fresh create failed' had no test. Fixed: BUSY test (c97b50b13), and in 2c9658cd7 a test using a zero RLIMIT_FSIZE that forces the fresh create to fail (fails open loudly, names the kept file, evidence intact, still prunes). A 0400-file case was NOT added (outcome platform-dependent).

trigger: a future edit weakens the assertion or moves the increment
classification_rationale: still_known > 0 was weak; the lexical gate's increment check was satisfied by a hoisted increment
summary: Fixed in c97b50b13: still_known >= kRows - 10 and a re-claim of an id on the damaged page must be Error not Claimed; the gate uses brace-matched block_after, requires exactly one increment, and has a hoist mutation row. Also move-assignment carry test and a docs/test-coverage.md row added.

trigger: an operator reads the figure as a guarantee
classification_rationale: an unreproducible '99.6%' figure from one reviewer experiment appeared in shipped docs and a code comment
summary: Replaced by a hedged statement in c97b50b13 (nearly every id still resolved with one damaged leaf page; interior or root damage costs many more). Also -journal, 'best effort' and prune-timing wording.

trigger: two agent processes on one data dir recover a corrupt file within the same second
classification_rationale: the 'never overwrites' guarantee was check-then-rename; rename() replaces its destination on POSIX and Windows
summary: Two agent processes recovering the same corrupt file in the same second (no instance lock exists) could destroy each other's quarantined evidence and split dedup onto an orphaned inode. Fixed in d04ccdc4c: the name is CLAIMED atomically with create_hard_link (EEXIST => next suffix) then the original name is dropped; falls back to check-then-rename only if the link fails for a reason other than EEXIST. Closure evidence: the security re-review ran 2000 rounds of two threads linking the same name, exactly one won every round (verified on macOS), plus a dangling-symlink-on-the-wanted-name test that passes ONLY on the link path (2c9658cd7). Residual (two daemons on one data dir; B can drop A's fresh store) is unsupported and documented. Windows untested.

trigger: a failing disk where every boot quarantines and the fresh create fails
classification_rationale: prune ran only after a successful retry so the keep-3 bound was conditional
summary: On a disk where the fresh create keeps failing, each boot added one more quarantined file with no prune. Also raised by sre. Fixed in d04ccdc4c: prune runs after any successful quarantine; pinned by the RLIMIT_FSIZE test (2c9658cd7). The residual junk files are small.

trigger: quarantine succeeds, then the fresh store cannot be created (disk full, permissions)
classification_rationale: the branch quarantine-ok-then-create-fails was undocumented, unnamed in the error and untested
summary: Error now names the kept file and says the history is lost (d04ccdc4c); docs describe the state; tested in 2c9658cd7. quarantined_total is deliberately NOT incremented there because yuzu.dedup_degraded already carries it (architect, enterprise-architect).

adjudicated_by: enterprise-architect (Fable-tier read-only validator, agent a1f88be82; not the change's author; independence ASSERTED, not enforced)
adjudication_rationale: ruled SHIP WITHOUT a durable marker: invariant 7 binds FAILURE observability and every degraded branch emits dedup_degraded=1; after a successful recovery there is no failure in effect; a marker with zero server consumers is a write nobody reads; the unit of work is a durable marker plus the first server consumer of yuzu.dedup_* (WS-11)
trigger: any agent restart after a corruption recovery
classification_rationale: the yuzu.dedup_quarantined tag is a per-process counter; invariant 7 says store failure MUST stay observable
summary: NOTE ON THE FACTS: the reporter listed I6 and I3; the recorder dropped I3 because the tag never presents a wrong result (it is documented as per-process and says so), leaving I6 (base MEDIUM); the independent adjudicator confirmed the non-gating reading (adjudicated_by). One agent restart after a recovery returns the heartbeat tag to 0 while up to 3 quarantined files remain; no server consumer of any yuzu.dedup_* tag exists (verified by grep in server/, gateway/, docs/prometheus). Documented honestly in command-dedup.md and security-hardening.md. NOT fixed in this PR: the enterprise-architect final review ruled ship-without: invariant 7 binds FAILURE observability (every degraded branch is loud), a durable marker with zero server consumers is a write nobody reads, the right unit of work is 'fleet consumer + durable marker' together (WS-11). CANDIDATE FOLLOW-UP, NOT FILED (owner approval needed).

trigger: a transient bad read of page 1 of a healthy file
classification_rationale: filed as a mandatory investigation: a transient bad read of page 1 (AV filter, FUSE, zero-filled read) makes SQLite report NOTADB on a healthy file
summary: SPECULATIVE as filed: no environment is known where SQLite returns NOTADB on a healthy agent data-dir file. Recorded at its derived band (I2 x E5 = MEDIUM) pending resolution; see the superseding row.

adjudicated_by: enterprise-architect (Fable-tier read-only validator, agent a1f88be82, summoned by the orchestrator; not the change's author; independence ASSERTED within this session, not enforced)
adjudication_rationale: final-gate ruling: UPHELD at LOW (I8, E5, likely). IMPACT is measured against the shipped baseline; the file is preserved aside and the old code would have been degraded for the same boot. A retry is wrong to add; not a ship condition.
trigger: a transient bad read of page 1 of a healthy file
classification_rationale: resolved: the file is MOVED ASIDE, not destroyed
summary: DE-ESCALATION from I2/MEDIUM to I8/LOW. The file is preserved byte-for-byte under .corrupt-<epoch> (an operator can restore it) and the fresh store protects the rest of the boot, whereas the old code stayed degraded for the whole boot; nothing is destroyed and nothing re-executes that would not have under the baseline. Epistemic status raised from speculative to likely (the NOTADB code path is real; the environmental trigger is still unnamed). A retry-once mitigation was REJECTED as wrong (a genuinely bad page 1 re-reads identically; boot latency on an unevidenced trigger); it would be reconsidered if a reproducible environment is found.

trigger: power loss between the claim and the sidecar moves
classification_rationale: SQLite discards an orphan -wal beside a missing main file
summary: A crash/power loss between the main-file claim and the sidecar moves loses the most recent WAL commits; the next boot finds no file and records nothing. The history was already unreadable, so accepted. Candidate follow-up: move sidecars before the main file. NOT FILED.

adjudicated_by: enterprise-architect (Fable-tier read-only validator, agent a1f88be82; not the change's author; independence ASSERTED, not enforced)
adjudication_rationale: the reporter labelled it MEDIUM but its facts derive HIGH (I3); recorded at the DERIVED band. REJECTED as a defect of this change: the same re-execution exists in the pre-change code (the file would not open and the agent stayed degraded), it is the owner-ruled trade-off R1, and the enterprise-architect found the framing fair and sufficient for a risk register
trigger: a crash that interrupts a command and corrupts the dedup store, then a redelivery
classification_rationale: the documented trade-off of owner ruling R1
summary: A command that crashed mid-execution alongside the corrupt store re-executes on redelivery. This is the OWNER-RULED, documented trade-off, no worse than the previous permanent-degraded state (the enterprise-architect final review: the exposure is bounded to commands dispatched before the corrupt boot and redelivered after it, whereas the baseline exposed the same commands AND every later one for the whole boot, so the docs' 'no worse' is an understatement). Whether a server-side guard exists for Destructive pairs was not traced. Rejected as a defect; recorded as an accepted residual for the customer risk register.

trigger: a Windows file holder without FILE_SHARE_DELETE at boot
classification_rationale: Windows leg untested; observable fail-open
summary: A sharing violation (AV, indexer, an old agent) on the main rename/delete leaves the agent degraded until restart; observable through dedup_degraded=1. Also cross-platform F2. Candidate follow-up: one short retry on Windows plus a Windows test leg. NOT FILED.

trigger: see summary
classification_rationale: UP-9 meta seed warns on a full disk; UP-10 a flapping disk loses the first corruption's evidence after 3 more recoveries; UP-12 planted names; UP-13/F4 symlinked db_path differs by OS (macOS link() follows, Linux does not); UP-14 bad_alloc inside noexcept handlers
summary: Recorded as accepted LOW/INFO residuals, each bounded and observable or requiring write access to the data directory. Clock-order distortion (UP-11, far-future or pre-NTP names) is documented in command-dedup.md.

trigger: an auditor inventories endpoint data
classification_rationale: the enterprise-readiness agent-side data inventory listed neither command_dedup.db nor its quarantined copies (item 6 reading; compliance judged it not one of the six required docs)
summary: Fixed in d04ccdc4c with a new inventory subsection; corrected in 2c9658cd7 (see docs-r4-uninstall-claim-false).

trigger: an operator or auditor relies on the inventory row as the erasure route
classification_rationale: my own round-3 inventory row said the file is removed with the data directory on uninstall
summary: False on 5 of 6 uninstall paths: the DEB, RPM and macOS uninstallers and a silent Windows uninstall keep the data directory (#5147); an interactive Windows uninstall removes it only on an explicit Yes. It would have concealed the real retention state from an auditor. Corrected in 2c9658cd7 in the inventory row and the quarantined-files row, and in the manual. A reasonable adjudicator could say MEDIUM (the stored content is mostly non-personal); not de-escalated.

trigger: a reader quotes the claim in a questionnaire
classification_rationale: I wrote that the stored frame carries up to 64 KiB of command output
summary: False for the normal path: the stored frame is make_final_frame (status, exit code, plugin result status, short error text; no streamed output, which is flushed as RUNNING frames); the 64 KiB is a cap on the whole frame. The security re-review read the same constant as supporting the claim: the DISAGREEMENT was settled by the orchestrator reading agent.cpp and confirmed by the enterprise-architect (verified). Corrected in 2c9658cd7 everywhere (manual, command-dedup.md, inventory, header comment); the files stay 'sensitive as a precaution'.

trigger: a reader of the docs
classification_rationale: 'next recovery' (prune timing, said wrong by 3 reviewers), exact wording of the hard-link fallback, uninstall/epoch conversion/path pattern/operator next steps, 'always active', split of the long manual bullet
summary: All fixed across d04ccdc4c and 2c9658cd7. upgrading.md (a historical WS-0 release note) deliberately NOT edited.

trigger: reverting the claim to check-then-rename leaves the old tests green
classification_rationale: the hard_link_count==1 and collision tests pass on either path; offered as closure evidence for UP-5 they would be false-greens
summary: Closure evidence for UP-5 is the 2000-round concurrent experiment (not kept) plus, from 2c9658cd7, a dangling-symlink-on-the-wanted-name test that passes only on the hard-link path, a create_hard_link file_exists pin test (every CI leg), and a rename-fallback test (a directory as the path). cross-platform raised the same gap.

trigger: two agent daemons on one data dir
classification_rationale: the docs' 'even against a second process' could be read as covering the live store
summary: The claim protects the quarantined EVIDENCE only; two daemons on one data dir are unsupported (no instance lock) and B can still drop A's fresh store. Clause added to the header comment, command-dedup.md and the manual ('Unsupported'). Architect raised the same.

trigger: a corrupt file restored from a backup at a looser mode; a stat error on a sidecar
classification_rationale: owner-only mode on the quarantined files; give-back failure unlogged; sidecar whose existence cannot be determined
summary: (sec F3) the quarantined main file and carried sidecars are set owner-only, best effort; (cross F2) a failed give-back of the claim is logged and the comment softened; (cpp-safety F3) a sidecar whose existence cannot be determined is removed rather than left beside the fresh store. All in 2c9658cd7.

trigger: an edit to the fallback branch
classification_rationale: the rename-fallback success arm and the give-back arm had no test
summary: Fallback success arm now tested (a directory as the path: link(2) fails with EPERM). NOT covered, recorded in docs/test-coverage.md: the give-back arm when remove(path) fails after a successful claim, the all-10,000-names refusal, the Windows link path and the ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS mapping, two real processes.

trigger: a refactor moves prune inside if (attempt) or reverts the claim
classification_rationale: prune placement and the hard-link claim were silently regressible
summary: Prune-after-failed-retry is pinned by the RLIMIT_FSIZE test; the hard-link claim by the dangling-symlink test. Remaining silent regressibles recorded: DbGuard-before-rename ordering (Windows), the is_corruption_rc mask / exact step set for the pragma steps.

trigger: the two copies diverge further
classification_rationale: echo_db.cpp's quarantine_corrupt_db is a separate copy
summary: OWNER DECISION: copy the helper rather than hoist. Echo lacks this code's no-overwrite claim and negative-epoch clamp, so the copies are drifting. Candidate follow-up: hoist both into agents/shared. NOT FILED.

trigger: a reader trusts the comment
classification_rationale: a header comment said the moved file keeps its mode while the code sets 0600; command-dedup.md still called the second-attempt branch untested
summary: Both fixed after the final review. VERDICT of the final review: ENDORSE, confidence high; no blocking condition.

trigger: a reader treats this run as a full CI-equivalent verification
classification_rationale: recorded deviations of this governance run
summary: (1) Gates 3 and the Gate 8 security/docs re-review first ran on c4aa020c2; fixes to their findings landed in c97b50b13, d04ccdc4c and 2c9658cd7 and the relevant domains were re-run on each fix diff. (2) Gates 4 and 6 ran TOGETHER on c97b50b13 (not sequentially), Gate 5 chaos ran with the Gate 8 re-review of d04ccdc4c. (3) NOT run: Linux and Windows builds, ASan/UBSan/TSan, /test (the pre-commit pipeline), the full meson test suite (only tests/yuzu_agent_tests, the lexical gate and tests/test_plugin_readmes.py), a manual agent boot against a corrupted file, the Windows leg of every new test. (4) The reviewers are model agents of this session; independence is asserted, not enforced. (5) Owner rulings R1 (no integrity scan) and R2 (keep the newest 3) were given by the user in this session; the copy-not-hoist decision as well. (6) Chaos scenarios CH-1..CH-9 are a design only; CH-3 and part of CH-1 were implemented as tests, CH-6 resolved by reasoning (see up-r3-7). (7) Follow-up issues were NOT filed (no owner approval).
